baseline:
epoll_ctl05 has exactly one assertion. Host run of the pinned prebuilt (/nix/store/hik6kb512ia3p14lc2vwzb292d4k306a-ltp-20260529/testcases/bin/epoll_ctl05, LTP 20260529, Linux 6.8.0-124-generic): 'epoll_ctl05.c:61: TPASS: epoll_ctl(..., EPOLL_CTL_ADD, ...) : ELOOP (40)', 1 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken. Per assertion: setup builds a chain of MAX_DEPTH=5 epoll instances over a pipe (ep1 monitors fd[0], ep2 monitors ep1, ... ep5 monitors ep4), then removes fd[0] from ep1, so all five epoll_ctl(ADD) calls in setup and the ADD/DEL bookkeeping must return 0; the single verified call, epoll_ctl(ep1, EPOLL_CTL_ADD, ep5), must return -1 with errno ELOOP(40), because it would close the cycle ep1 -> ep5 -> ep4 -> ep3 -> ep2 -> ep1.

The test samples one point of a broader rule, so I measured the whole boundary on the host with a purpose-built probe (/tmp/eploop2.c, one case per fresh process -- cyclic epoll references keep struct files alive past close(), so cases sharing an address space contaminate each other and my first single-process probe produced wrong numbers):

- Closing a cycle returns ELOOP(40) at every constructible length: the epoll_ctl05 shape with n = 2, 3, 4 and 5 all give ELOOP, as do bare epoll-only cycles of 2, 3, 4 and 5. Cycle rejection is therefore NOT a consequence of depth -- a 2-cycle is detected at walk depth 0. LTP's choice of 5 is just the longest chain that can be built at all.
- Self-add is a different error: epoll_ctl(ep, ADD, ep) returns EINVAL(22), not ELOOP, and so does epoll_ctl(ep, ADD, dup(ep)) -- the comparison is on file-description identity, not the fd number. So a cycle of length 1 is EINVAL and a cycle of length >= 2 is ELOOP; the two rules are independent and a fix must not fold them together.
- Nesting a *different* epoll is legal: ADD of a fresh epoll b into a fresh epoll a returns 0. The rule is about cycles, not about epoll-in-epoll.
- Depth is a separate bound with the same errno: a pure epoll chain accepts up to 5 nested instances and rejects the 6th with ELOOP(40) (measured with /tmp/epdepth.c, which has no ordinary file in the graph so Linux's reverse_path_check cannot be the source). Chains over a pipe agree: 4 epolls + 1 more succeeds, 5 epolls + 1 more gives ELOOP. This is epoll_ctl04's assertion, out of scope for this run, and it explains why epoll_ctl04 accepts either EINVAL or ELOOP -- older kernels returned EINVAL from reverse_path_check for the depth case.

man 2 epoll_ctl could not be read: man pages are stripped in this container and both man7.org and www.man7.org are blocked by the fetch tool. The specification is instead established from the kernel source at four versions (see linux_reference) plus the measurements above, which is stronger evidence than the man page for the boundaries that matter here.
failing_assertion:
'epoll_ctl05.c:61: TFAIL: epoll_ctl(..., EPOLL_CTL_ADD, ...) succeeded', with 0 passed / 1 failed / 0 broken, from a selector boot at base e8f2b9ca6 (/tmp/zyw0OP-qemu-verbose.log:52-57). Asterinas's actual wrong value is 0: TST_EXP_FAIL expands to TST_EXP_FAIL_SILENT_(TST_RET == 0, ...) (include/tst_test_macros.h:399-425, 462-496), whose ' succeeded' message is emitted only on the TST_RET == 0 arm -- the two other failure arms print ' invalid retval %ld' or ' expected ELOOP', so the wording pins the return value to exactly 0 rather than to a wrong errno.

broken == 0 is the other half of the observation: it means setup did not tst_brk, so all five nested epoll_ctl(ADD) calls and the EPOLL_CTL_DEL of the pipe succeeded. Asterinas therefore already supports epoll nesting to depth 5 and only the cycle rejection is absent -- the failure is not a missing epoll feature.

The first boot showed only kirk's one-line 'epoll_ctl05: fail' (qemu.log:43). Since libkirk/ui.py:138-148 classifies on results.failed before results.broken, that line alone already implied a TFAIL rather than a TBROK, but to make the assertion observed rather than derived I temporarily inverted the KIRK_VERBOSE guard in test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/run_ltp_test.sh:23 to force kirk --verbose, re-ran, and reverted it. The worktree is clean again (git status shows only the untracked .osdk/).

impl.note: EpollFile::add_interest -- the whole error-path set is the single EEXIST check at 100-105; nothing inspects the target's type or walks the epoll graph
EpollFile::control -- resolves the target fd at 72-74 and dispatches to add/del/mod; the only place holding both the epoll file (&self) and the target Arc<dyn FileLike>
sys_epoll_ctl tail -- downcasts epfd to EpollFile and calls control(); the only caller
ReadySet::push -- holds the entries SpinLock<_, LocalIrqDisabled> guard across the unconditional self.pollee.notify(IoEvents::IN) at 330; this is what turns a cycle into a self-deadlock
impl events::Observer<IoEvents> for Observer -- on_events calls ready_set.push(self), so notification is a direct synchronous call into the parent epoll

interest set is Mutex<BTreeSet<EntryHolder>> keyed on EntryKey{fd, KeyableWeak<dyn FileLike>}; Entry::update registers the parent's PollHandle on the child via file.poll(.., Some(poller)); Entry::file_weak() is pub(super) and upgradeable, so file.rs can already walk the graph
SyncSubject::notify_observers -- calls observer.on_events synchronously while holding its own observers SpinLock, so the propagation chain is real recursion, not a deferred queue

root_cause:
Asterinas has no epoll interest-graph validation of any kind. grep -niE 'ELOOP|MAX_NESTS|loop_check|nest|cycle' over kernel/src/events/epoll/ and kernel/src/syscall/epoll.rs returns zero hits, and ELOOP appears nowhere in the epoll path.

The mechanism is a straight fall-through. sys_epoll_ctl (kernel/src/syscall/epoll.rs:85-95) resolves epfd, downcasts it to EpollFile, and calls control() -- it never resolves the target fd itself and so never compares the two files. EpollFile::control (file.rs:65-85) resolves the target at 72-74 and dispatches to add_interest. add_interest (file.rs:87-128) has exactly one error path: the EEXIST test at 100-105 asking whether EntryKey{fd, KeyableWeak(file)} is already in the interest set. In epoll_ctl05 ep1's interest set is empty at that moment (setup deleted fd[0] from it), so the key is absent, Entry::new + interest.insert(entry) run at 107-117, and add_interest returns Ok(()). sys_epoll_ctl:95 maps that to SyscallReturn::Return(0), which is the 0 the test observes. Because EpollFile implements Pollable via self.ready.poll (file.rs:255-259), the target epoll is a perfectly ordinary pollable FileLike as far as add_interest can tell, so nothing distinguishes it from a pipe.

The wrong errno is the visible symptom; the created cycle is the actual defect, and in Asterinas it is a CPU hang rather than a mere inefficiency. Entry::update (entry.rs:155-166) registers the parent's PollHandle on the child by calling file.poll(events, Some(&mut inner.poller)), so a parent epoll becomes an observer on the child epoll's Pollee. Delivery is synchronous all the way down: Pollee::notify (process/signal/poll.rs:174-178) calls SyncSubject::notify_observers, which invokes observer.on_events directly (events/subject.rs:126-153); Observer::on_events (entry.rs:280-284) calls self.ready_set.push(self). And ReadySet::push (entry.rs:307-331) takes the entries SpinLock<VecDeque<Weak<Entry>>, LocalIrqDisabled> at 320 and still holds that guard when it calls self.pollee.notify(IoEvents::IN) at 330 -- unconditionally, even when the entry was already marked ready, per the 'Wake the poller anyway' comment at 327-329, so the is_ready flag does not damp the chain.

Consequence: one event propagates parent-ward as an unbroken recursive call chain, each hop holding one epoll's IRQ-disabled spinlock. Around a cycle that chain re-enters the epoll it started from and tries to re-acquire a spinlock the same CPU already holds with interrupts disabled -- a self-deadlock that hangs the CPU, reachable by unprivileged userspace with about ten lines of C. epoll_ctl05 does not trigger it only because its pipe is empty and was removed from ep1, so no event ever enters the cycle; adding a write to fd[1] before closing the loop turns the same accepted epoll_ctl into a hang. This is precisely the hazard Linux names in its own locking comment (fs/eventpoll.c:61-68: cycles 'could lead to deadlock').
invariant:
The epoll interest graph -- the directed graph whose nodes are epoll file descriptions and whose edges run from an epoll to each epoll registered in its interest set -- must remain acyclic at all times, and every operation that would add an edge closing a cycle must be refused rather than performed. Refusal is reported as ELOOP, except that the degenerate cycle of length 1 (a file description registered in its own interest set) is refused with EINVAL. Acyclicity is a structural precondition of the notification machinery, not a courtesy: event delivery walks edges parent-ward synchronously while holding per-epoll locks, so a cycle makes that walk non-terminating and makes the lock order ill-defined. It follows that the check must be performed before the edge is inserted, and must be a reachability question about the whole graph -- 'is the epoll being inserted into reachable from the target?' -- not a test of the two endpoints and not a count of anything local to one node.

The companion rule, enforced at the same point and by the same walk, is that the graph's depth is bounded: no path may contain more than EP_MAX_NESTS = 4 epoll-to-epoll edges, i.e. at most 5 epoll instances may be chained, and an operation that would exceed the bound is refused with ELOOP. This bound exists because the same parent-ward walk consumes kernel stack per level. It is stated here because it belongs to the same invariant and the same enforcement point; it is the assertion of epoll_ctl04, which stays blocked and out of scope for this run.

Two negative clauses matter as much as the positive one. Registering a *different* epoll file description is legal and must keep working -- epoll nesting is a supported feature and the rule constrains cycles and depth, never epoll-in-epoll as such. And a cycle of length 1 must not be reported as ELOOP: identity is a distinct rule with a distinct errno, so the reachability walk must not treat the target itself as a match.
owning_layer:
The epoll interest-graph layer -- the epoll module itself, kernel/src/events/epoll/, entered through EpollFile::control (file.rs:65-85) as the admission gate for every edge. Not the syscall entry layer, and not VFS or the file-description layer.

This is the one placement decision worth arguing, because the neighbouring epoll defect diagnosed on this same base commit went the other way. run-rVlQYu's epoll_ctl02 fix correctly puts its two checks at the syscall entry seam, since both are answerable from the two file handles alone: 'are these the same file description?' and 'does this file description support polling?'. The ELOOP rule is categorically different -- it cannot be answered from the two endpoints, because whether an edge closes a cycle is a property of every edge already in the graph. Only code with access to EpollFile::interest, which is a private Mutex<BTreeSet<EntryHolder>> (file.rs:42), can answer it, and only by walking transitively. sys_epoll_ctl has no way to reach that state and should not be given one; pushing a graph walk into the syscall layer would mean exposing the interest set, which is exactly the encapsulation the module has today.

Within the epoll module the gate must be EpollFile::control rather than add_interest, for the same reason Linux checks before ep_find: the graph must be validated before any mutation, and control is the single point that holds both the epoll file (&self) and the resolved target Arc<dyn FileLike> (file.rs:72-74). Placing the walk inside add_interest after the EEXIST test would also invert Linux's error precedence, which resolves ELOOP before EEXIST.

Asterinas's abstractions line up with Linux's closely here, so there is little to reconcile: EpollFile is the counterpart of struct eventpoll, the interest BTreeSet of ep->rbr, and EntryKey{fd, KeyableWeak<dyn FileLike>} of struct epoll_filefd -- the same (fd, file) pair Linux's ep_find keys on. The one structural gap is that Asterinas keeps only downward edges: an epoll knows what it monitors, but a file has no back-link to the epolls monitoring it, so there is no equivalent of Linux's ep->refs / f_ep. That gap is why the fix should be expressed as a downward reachability walk from the target (which Asterinas can do) rather than a copy of Linux v6.17's two-directional depth computation (which it cannot without adding back-links). Cycle detection needs only the downward walk; only the exact depth bound needs the upward half, which is another reason to keep epoll_ctl04 out of this run.

One more property of this layer that the fix inherits: the rule is a lock-ordering precondition for the notification path in kernel/src/events/epoll/entry.rs, not just an errno. Linux says so explicitly in its locking comment (fs/eventpoll.c:61-76): the global epnested_mutex exists so the tree walk cannot race, 'and since we disallow cycles of epoll file descriptors, this ensures that the mutexes are well-ordered.' Whatever guards the walk in Asterinas must likewise make two concurrent inserts, A into B and B into A, unable to both observe an acyclic graph and both proceed.
linux_reference:
Read fs/eventpoll.c at v6.8, v6.11, v6.14 and v6.17 (raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux). Linux enforces this in the epoll implementation itself, in do_epoll_ctl -- above VFS, above any filesystem, and inside the epoll module rather than in the syscall wrapper. It is not a VFS rule and has no vfs_* helper, which is the structural reason the Asterinas check belongs in kernel/src/events/epoll/ rather than at the syscall entry.

Order in do_epoll_ctl (v6.11 fs/eventpoll.c:2257-2405, unchanged in substance at v6.8/6.14/6.17): fdget both fds for -EBADF; then 'error = -EPERM; if (!file_can_poll(tf.file))'; then 'error = -EINVAL; if (f.file == tf.file || !is_file_epoll(f.file))' -- a struct file pointer comparison, which is why dup(epfd) is EINVAL too; then, gated on is_file_epoll(tf.file), 'error = -ELOOP; if (ep_loop_check(ep, tep) != 0) goto error_tgt_fput;'; and only then ep_find and the per-op switch yielding -EEXIST / -ENOENT. So ELOOP precedes EEXIST, and the self-add EINVAL precedes ELOOP. The loop check is also gated on the target being an epoll, which is the cheap early-out Asterinas should copy.

The check itself was reworked between v6.14 and v6.17, and the container kernel (6.8.0-124-generic) behaves like the reworked version, so v6.17 is the reference to follow. v6.8/v6.11/v6.14 ep_loop_check_proc (v6.11:2102-2139) walks the target's rbr and sets error = -1 when 'ep_tovisit == inserting_into || depth > EP_MAX_NESTS'; a pure depth violation with an ordinary file at the leaf instead fell through to reverse_path_check during ep_insert, which returns -EINVAL (v6.8:1536-1539) -- that is the historical EINVAL epoll_ctl04 still accepts. v6.17 ep_loop_check_proc (2153-2190) instead returns the subtree depth, or INT_MAX on 'ep_tovisit == inserting_into || depth > EP_MAX_NESTS', and ep_loop_check (2219-2237) combines it with an upward walk: 'depth = ep_loop_check_proc(to, 0); if (depth > EP_MAX_NESTS) return -1;' then ep_get_upwards_depth_proc over ep->refs, returning -1 when 'depth+1+upwards_depth > EP_MAX_NESTS'. Both arms surface as -ELOOP at the call site, which matches my measurements exactly: cycles rejected at any length, and 5 chained epolls accepted while 6 give ELOOP (EP_MAX_NESTS = 4 counts edges, v6.17:94).

The cycle and depth arms are genuinely independent, and for epoll_ctl05 it is the cycle arm that fires. Tracing ep_loop_check(ep1, ep5): inserting_into = ep1, then the walk ep5 -> ep4 -> ep3 -> ep2 finds ep1 in ep2's set at depth 3, below EP_MAX_NESTS, so the 'ep_tovisit == inserting_into' test is what returns the error. My bare 2-cycle measurement makes the same point from the other side: it is caught at depth 0.

The most useful thing in the file is the locking comment at fs/eventpoll.c:44-83, which states the rationale rather than the mechanism: epnested_mutex is taken 'when inserting an epoll fd onto another epoll fd. We do this so that we walk the epoll tree and ensure that this insertion does not create a cycle of epoll file descriptors, which could lead to deadlock. We need a global mutex to prevent two simultaneous inserts (A into B and B into A) from racing and constructing a cycle without either insert observing that it is going to.' And: 'Since we disallow cycles of epoll file descriptors, this ensures that the mutexes are well-ordered.' Linux treats acyclicity as the precondition that makes its lock order sound -- the same role it plays for ReadySet::push in Asterinas, and the reason to read this as a soundness fix rather than an errno fix.
other_callers:
For the check's entry point, nobody else: grep over kernel/src for '.control(' and 'add_interest' finds sys_epoll_ctl (kernel/src/syscall/epoll.rs:93) as the only caller of EpollFile::control, and control (file.rs:78) as the only caller of add_interest, the cgroupfs '.control()' hits being an unrelated method. Linux agrees -- ep_loop_check has exactly one call site, in do_epoll_ctl. So the guard itself is genuinely epoll-local and a check at that one gate is defensible rather than merely convenient; there is no second syscall that can add an edge to the interest graph.

What is emphatically not epoll-local is the defect's blast radius, and this is the reason to fix the graph rather than the errno. The corrupted state is consumed by the shared notification machinery, which every pollable file in the kernel drives: any file whose Pollee::notify fires -- pipes, sockets, ttys, eventfd, timerfd, signalfd, inotify, and every device -- enters the parent-ward chain through Observer::on_events (entry.rs:280-284) into ReadySet::push (entry.rs:307-331). Once a cycle exists in the graph, the first event delivered from any of those sources into any epoll on the cycle hits the self-deadlock, so the victim of an unchecked epoll_ctl is not epoll but whichever unrelated subsystem happens to deliver the next event on that CPU. Notification also reaches push from IRQ-adjacent context (the SpinLock is LocalIrqDisabled precisely for that reason), so the hang is not confined to the thread that built the cycle.

Two internal paths through the same code are worth naming as unaffected, since they bound the fix. EpollFile::pop_multi_ready (file.rs:210-246) is the only internal caller of del_interest (file.rs:232) and only ever removes entries, so it cannot create an edge. And the epoll_wait side does not recurse through nested epolls at all: Entry::poll (entry.rs:116-150) calls file.poll, which for a child epoll is EpollFile::poll -> ReadySet::poll -> check_io_events (entry.rs:341-354), a single non-empty test on that child's own deque rather than a descent into its interest set. So the wait path is already safe against deep nesting, and the recursion hazard is specific to the notify path -- a fix must guard the graph, not the wait loop.

Finally, two adjacent tests share this enforcement point and are useful as scope markers. epoll_ctl04 (all.txt line 186) asserts the depth bound and stays blocked; a downward-walk fix will likely not turn it green on its own, since the exact bound needs the upward half Asterinas has no back-links for. epoll_ctl02 is being fixed on a separate unmerged branch (run-rVlQYu) and its self-add EINVAL check must stay ordered before this ELOOP path; the two do not conflict at base e8f2b9ca6, which contains neither.
suggested_direction:
Add a reachability check to the epoll module and call it from EpollFile::control before any mutation. No new subsystem and no change to the file-description or VFS layers.

Shape: in EpollFile::control (kernel/src/events/epoll/file.rs:65-85), after resolving the target file at 72-74 and only for the Add arm, early-out unless the target downcasts to EpollFile -- mirroring Linux's is_file_epoll(tf.file) gate, so the common case pays one downcast. When it does, ask whether `self` is reachable from the target by walking downward edges, and return ELOOP if so. Everything needed is already in place: EpollFile::interest is a Mutex<BTreeSet<EntryHolder>> (file.rs:42) that iterates today in dump_proc_fdinfo (file.rs:294), and Entry::file_weak() is pub(super) (entry.rs:193-196), so file.rs can upgrade each KeyableWeak<dyn FileLike> into an Arc and downcast_ref::<EpollFile>() exactly as sys_epoll_ctl does at kernel/src/syscall/epoll.rs:91. Entry::file() itself is private to entry.rs, so use file_weak() and skip entries whose weak reference is dead rather than widening that method.

Four correctness constraints, each measured on the host:

1. Compare file-description identity, not fd numbers -- the interest set is keyed on (fd, weak file) and the same file can appear under several fds. Arc::ptr_eq against `self` is the analogue of Linux's `ep_tovisit == inserting_into`.
2. Do not treat the target itself as a match. Self-add must stay EINVAL, not ELOOP (measured: errno 22), which is a separate rule owned by the entry path and landing on the run-rVlQYu branch. Start the reachability test at the target's children, exactly as ep_loop_check_proc does.
3. Terminate on already-visited nodes. Because the graph may already contain a cycle from an earlier unchecked insert, and because a DAG can reach the same node by several paths, the walk needs a visited set (a small Vec of raw pointers or a BTreeSet of KeyableWeak is enough) -- this is what Linux's ep->gen / loop_check_gen generation counter buys. Without it the walk can itself fail to terminate, which would replace one hang with another. Bounding the walk by EP_MAX_NESTS = 4 as a belt-and-braces limit is cheap and matches Linux's constant.
4. Serialize concurrent inserts. Two threads adding A into B and B into A can each observe an acyclic graph and both proceed, constructing a cycle neither saw -- the exact race Linux's global epnested_mutex exists to prevent (fs/eventpoll.c:61-68). A single module-level Mutex in kernel/src/events/epoll/, taken only on the Add-of-an-epoll path so the ordinary case never touches it, is the direct analogue. Note the walk must not hold one epoll's `interest` Mutex while locking a child's, or two opposite-direction walks deadlock on the interest mutexes themselves; take each node's lock, copy out the epoll children, release, then descend -- or rely on the global mutex to make nested acquisition safe. Prefer the former, since it keeps the lock discipline local and does not depend on the graph already being acyclic.

Expected result: epoll_ctl05's single assertion returns ELOOP. Verify with the default configuration (no workdir override), since the pool entry is in all.txt. Regression-check that legal nesting still works -- epoll_ctl01/03, epoll_create01/02, epoll_create1_01/02, epoll01, epoll_wait01/03/04/07 and epoll_pwait01/02/04/05/06 are already enabled and exercise the epoll paths this touches, and epoll_ctl05's own setup is itself a 5-deep nesting test that must keep succeeding. Leave epoll_ctl04 commented out: its depth bound needs the upward walk over back-links that Asterinas does not have, and enabling it is a separate round.
